bibl.title: The Fourteenth Catechetical Homily — ܡܐܡܪܐ ܕܐܪܒܥܐ
The third homily on baptism
bibl.author: Theodore of Mopsuestia — ܬܐܕܘܪܘܤ ܡܦܫܩܢܐ

noteGrp.note: On the meaning of baptism and post-baptismal anointment. Baptism is a symbol of the second birth, while the real second birth will take place after the common resurrection from the dead. Baptism is also participation in the death and resurrection of Christ. The baptized symbolically receive death with Christ through baptism to participate in His resurrection. The baptismal formula is “So-and-so is baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” After baptism, the newly baptized put on white and radiant garments, which symbolizes the light of the future world. The baptized receive the last anointment of the forehead, which alludes to the descent of the Holy Spirit upon Jesus, coming out of the waters of the river Jordan.
